title: Phase 6: move Pilobol.us and Threat Intelligence into the new Papyrus accounts
description:
## Goal
Pilobol.us and Threat Intelligence, the two sites already on the new Papyrus template pattern in the LEGACY account (335163751677), run in papyrus-production (712236451410) with their own new backends, data copied across, Google sign-in working, hostnames switched with records written by hand in the legacy zones, and the legacy copies retired by Ryan. Papyrus has two environments only (papyrus-staging 494166748521, papyrus-production 712236451410); papyrus-development is being removed and is never used here.

## Scope
- Pilobol.us (Markus static): CMS app dv0pdx67fk80m + reader app dssc97s4q5kgk, stack amplify-app-shell-pilobol-us-cms, repo AnthusAI/Pilobol.us, hosts pilobol.us (reader), newsroom.pilobol.us (CMS, newsroom at /), staging.pilobol.us; zone Z09961547QX1VHIXOBD7 (legacy); Google project 472527967203.
- Threat Intelligence (Pretext): app dzefa11i80jyq, stack amplify-app-shell-threat-intelligence-cms, repo AnthusAI/Threat-Intelligence, hosts threat-intelligence.anth.us and threat-intelligence-staging.anth.us on the SHARED root anth.us (zone Z02552332GG6AM25SFP73; Anth.us production d2hbn1ig6nqyhy shares it); Google project 778847915037. The OLD TI app d3on1y5vlrxmam is inert pending its two-week sign-off.
- Out of scope: Anth.us (last, Ryan), the other anth.us apps, moving any DNS zone, papyrus-development, SCPs on legacy.

## Decisions already made (Ryan, 2026-10-09/10)
Two environments only; all Papyrus-based sites leave legacy; DNS zones STAY in legacy so every cutover needs manual records in the legacy zones (recipe: PPY-52d455 plan comment cc25db); p.apyr.us (Phase 5, PPY-d1cc15) is the reference run; Ryan deletes retired resources; account creation needs Ryan's approval; never risk legacy access, no SCPs on legacy.

## Order
P6-01 first; then Pilobol.us (P6-02 to P6-07), Threat Intelligence (P6-08 to P6-13) can start its domain-free build once P6-02 has proven the pattern; DNS tickets P6-06 and P6-12 wait for the p.apyr.us cutover result (PPY-52d455, the cross-account association behaviour is unproven until then); P6-14 closes. Anth.us is a later phase.

## Sub-tasks (label phase-6; estimates in agent-days)
See the assessment comment on this ticket for the recommendations, risks and what Ryan must decide. Total about 17 agent-days, critical path about 10, plus a 7-day soak (Pilobol.us) and the two-week sign-off (TI).

## Assessment (2026-10-10; read-only AWS on legacy 335163751677, papyrus-production 712236451410, papyrus-staging 494166748521 with the account asserted before each call; public DNS lookups; nothing written anywhere except these Kanbus tickets)

### Ticket map (children of this ticket, label phase-6, estimates in agent-days)
P6-01 PPY-f675ec pre-flight and baselines (1) > P6-02 PPY-b0d5d3 Pilobol.us apps in production (2) > P6-03 PPY-3b64e5 Google (0.5) > P6-04 PPY-1f7a92 copy + reader on the new backend + byte parity (1.5) > P6-05 PPY-aeac36 staging (1) > P6-06 PPY-fd17b7 DNS cutover, three hosts (1.5, also blocked by PPY-52d455) > P6-07 PPY-514d54 retire (1, also blocked by PPY-343fea, 7-day soak).
TI: P6-08 PPY-5f34d8 app in production (2, after P6-02) > P6-09 PPY-b41a11 Google (0.5) > P6-10 PPY-7995be copy + fidelity (1.5) > P6-11 PPY-bb6929 throwaway-prefix proof on anth.us + staging (1) > P6-12 PPY-77e931 DNS cutover + Anth.us proof (2, also blocked by PPY-52d455) > P6-13 PPY-c7b06c archive + retire (1, also blocked by PPY-343fea, two-week sign-off). P6-14 PPY-753bfb close-out (0.5).
Total about 17.5 agent-days; critical path about 10.5 (TI builds overlap Pilobol.us after P6-02); plus the 7-day and two-week waits. No existing Phase 6 placeholder existed under PPY-1f1489, so this is new.

### Q1 Rehearse in papyrus-staging first? Recommendation: NO. Build directly in production (as p.apyr.us), de-risk with the p.apyr.us run and one small throwaway test.
- papyrus-staging is empty and NOT bootstrapped (no CDKToolkit, no stacks, no apps, no OIDC provider). A rehearsal costs per site: bootstrap + OIDC provider (once), a full backend (about 70 IAM roles, the AppSync 429 throttle in a fresh account), a GitHub App authorization for a third account, a Google client or extra URIs, a second data copy and a second set of baselines. It also cannot rehearse the dangerous part: the real hostnames. A hostname lives on one association at a time, so staging could only hold throwaway names.
- What actually carries risk is (a) DNS in the legacy zones and (b) the shared root anth.us. Both are cheaper to prove otherwise: p.apyr.us (PPY-52d455) is the reference run for the cross-account association and the one-record switch (R1); and P6-11 proves the shared-root behaviour with a THROWAWAY prefix `p6-rehearsal` on the new TI app in production (a new validation CNAME `_<new>.anth.us` in the legacy zone, no host record), then deletes it. That shows, with the real artifact and no real hostname, that a second account can hold an association on anth.us beside six legacy ones, that the validation tokens coexist, and that nothing changes for the other apps. Cost: 3 DNS writes and one association, about 0.5 day inside P6-11.
- The first sites are pre-production (Pilobol.us hard cutover with brief downtime accepted, TI too), the legacy apps stay intact as rollback until soak ends, and the order (Pilobol.us first, TI second, Anth.us last) is itself the rehearsal ladder.
- Decision for Ryan only if he wants a rehearsal anyway: staging would need a new approval for the bootstrap; I recommend against.

### Q2 Data copy (read-only counts today)
- Pilobol.us (backend amplify-dv0pdx67fk80m-main-branch-0f2f45caa3, API sqbda7ammrcurjmog54uo4wmky): Item 21, PublishedItem 18, MediaAsset 13, PublishedMediaAsset 12, ModelAttachment 2, Message 2, MessageThread 1 (everything else 0; 1 admin user, not copied). S3 media bucket: 112 objects, 20,466,255 bytes: media/ 13, newsroom/ 2, preview/ 97. Copy media/ and newsroom/ (15 objects); skip preview/ (regenerated by staging builds) and, unless Ryan objects, Message/MessageThread. The reader exports published items at build time as a guest, so there is no reader data; the reader env vars PAPYRUS_GRAPHQL_ENDPOINT, PAPYRUS_IDENTITY_POOL_ID, PAPYRUS_MEDIA_BUCKET must be switched to the new backend and compared with the new outputs (a reader left on the legacy backend would produce identical bytes and hide the mistake), then byte-parity against the live reader (23 to 63 paths, status, content-type, cache-control, sha256).
- Threat Intelligence (source = the LEGACY new-template backend a099beb80d, API otvp3nyxcff7rluvi2jfkf7vzq, already converted to Markus): Edition 1, PublishedEdition 1, EditionItem 18, PublishedEditionItem 18, Item 20, PublishedItem 18, MediaAsset 24, PublishedMediaAsset 24, NewsroomSection 6, Tag 8, ItemTag 24 = 162 rows; media bucket 65 objects, 160,572,044 bytes (14 mp4). The research data (Reference 1866, SemanticRelation 3258, ... corpora 88 MB, 1004 objects 254 MB) exists only in the inert OLD backend and stays archive-only; P6-13 archives it before the old backend is deleted.
- Both via `papyrus ops content copy-backend` cross-account (profiles legacy -> papyrus-production, `--expect-*-account`, `--s3-transfer stream`), dry run, Ryan's apply, idempotent re-run (0 changes), per-row manifest hashes, S3 key/size/ETag, byte compares, source unchanged. Wall time is minutes for both (tiny), unlike p.apyr.us (80 minutes for S3).

### Q3 Cognito domain prefix uniqueness, and the Google client
- A Cognito hosted-UI prefix is unique per region ACROSS ALL AWS accounts. Facts: legacy pool t1A6sJX55 (TI) holds `papyrus-threat-intelligence` (resolves in DNS); legacy Pilobol.us pool vyTCcLVQK still uses the auto-generated `69a74c507e157f784c3c` (its env var says `papyrus-pilobol-us-cms` but no apply flag was ever set, and that name does not resolve: free); old retired pools use hex names; production already holds `papyrus-p-apyr-us`.
- Options for TI: (A) a different prefix in production now, additive on the Google client, legacy keeps working through the sign-off; (B) delete the legacy domain first and reuse the name: breaks live sign-in, leaves a window where another account could take the name, and needs a second backend deploy. RECOMMENDATION: A. Prefixes: Pilobol.us `papyrus-pilobol-us-cms` (free; set `cms.applyCognitoDomainPrefix` true on the fresh pool; never run a legacy deploy with the apply flag, or legacy claims it), TI `papyrus-threat-intelligence-cms` (free today). If a name turns out taken, add `-prod`.
- Google: keep the EXISTING per-site client (project 472527967203 and 778847915037) and ADD the two Cognito-domain entries per site (JavaScript origin + `/oauth2/idpresponse`). Site hostnames never appear in Google. Keep the legacy entries until retirement (rollback keeps working), then remove them. Reasons: no new project, no new verification, no secret rotation, reversible. Watch the 10-unverified-domain limit per project: each Cognito prefix counts, so Ryan prunes entries of retired pools first. A NEW client would only add work (new secret, new SSM values, no benefit). The SSM secret path in the new account is /amplify/<newAppId>/main-branch-<sha512(appId+branch)[:10]>/ ; values move by pipe, never printed.

### Q4 DNS approach (zones stay in legacy; the p.apyr.us recipe)
- Pilobol.us (zone Z09961547QX1VHIXOBD7): three separate associations (pilobol.us on the reader; newsroom.pilobol.us and staging.pilobol.us on the CMS), three A aliases, three validation CNAMEs, NO other records (no MX): add three new validation CNAMEs (each association has its own token), wait AVAILABLE, check with `curl --resolve`, then one UPSERT of each A alias (HostedZoneId Z2FDTNDATAQYW2) in the order staging, newsroom, apex. Restore batches pre-written; the legacy `_08824...`, `_2ead...`, `_4bb4...` records stay until retirement.
- TI (zone Z02552332GG6AM25SFP73, 35 records): CNAME threat-intelligence and threat-intelligence-staging (TTL 500) -> dsdc44yor9rfm.cloudfront.net, plus the shared `_61eb...` validation record. PATH 1 (if PPY-52d455 shows R1 passes): create the new association, add the new `_<new>` CNAME, wait AVAILABLE, UPSERT the two CNAMEs. PATH 2 (proven 2026-10-08, about 6 minutes down): delete the legacy association first. 
- Anth.us and the other four apps (apricity, babulus, tactus, primus) cannot change: separate associations in a separate account, the zone is touched by exactly four names (the new validation CNAME and the two host CNAMEs; nothing else), the legacy `_61eb` token belongs to the legacy account and is never touched. P6-12 proves it before/after with the Anth.us hashes (95aa2bea..., c3b45f58..., 3ac5c9d0...), cert serial 4011E199..., `get-domain-association` diff for d2hbn1ig6nqyhy, `list-domain-associations` of the five other apps and a zone diff.
- Open mechanism risks: R1 (cross-account same-name association, unproven until PPY-52d455 B1) and D2 (deleting the legacy association later may delete the host records by name: retire tickets wait for PPY-343fea's evidence or run with restore batches ready).

### Q5 Order
Pilobol.us first (simplest: static reader, no shared root, no MX, 21 items), TI second (shared root, video, Pretext), Anth.us last (production, Ryan's rule). TI's domain-free build can start once P6-02 has shown the pattern; both cutovers wait for the p.apyr.us result.

### Q6 Constraints from the 'Rearrange AWS accounts' session
Never risk legacy access; no SCPs on legacy; all legacy writes limited to named DNS records (and, in PATH 2 only, one association) with Ryan's yes each; Ryan deletes retired resources via human runbooks (P6-07, P6-13); account creation not needed (papyrus-staging unused, papyrus-development never used).

### Risks
R1 and D2 (above); GitHub App must be authorized for papyrus-production on two more repos (and the repos are shared with the legacy apps: a push builds both); console connect overwrites buildSpec and env vars; AppSync 429 in production when two backends deploy together (deploy one at a time); Pilobol.us staging defects PPY-35a1fb and PPY-cb27a6 still open; Cognito prefix claimed by an accidental legacy deploy; SSO expiry mid-copy (idempotent); validation CNAME not added within minutes of the stack update; TI GithubCiRole trust widening to refs/heads/staging; Google unverified-domain limit; users do not move (re-sign-in and group assignment); the committed infra/site.json differs from what production needs until the cutover PR.

### What needs Ryan
Answers to the questions below; SSO; each stack deploy yes; one console sitting per app (GitHub App authorization for papyrus-production on AnthusAI/Pilobol.us and AnthusAI/Threat-Intelligence, connect, staging branch); Google console edits (4 entries, pruning); apply yes for each data copy and the editing freezes; each legacy zone write; go/no-go for the three Pilobol.us hosts and the two TI hosts; sign-in checks as editor and non-editor; all deletions (P6-07, P6-13); the names of TI's two editors.

### Open questions for Ryan
1. Cognito prefixes `papyrus-pilobol-us-cms` and `papyrus-threat-intelligence-cms` (additive Google entries, legacy kept): OK?
2. No papyrus-staging rehearsal; the throwaway `p6-rehearsal` prefix test in P6-11 instead (3 DNS writes in the shared anth.us zone, one new validation CNAME kept forever): OK?
3. Pilobol.us: skip the 3 Message/MessageThread rows and preview/ objects: OK?
4. If Amplify refuses a second account's same-name association (R1): accept the PATH 2 downtime (about 5 to 15 minutes per host) for Pilobol.us and TI?
5. Prune old Google entries (retired pools) to stay under the unverified-domain limit?
6. Names of TI's two editors (never in the repo).
7. Freeze windows: legacy newsrooms read-only during each delta copy and cutover.

comments.text:
[publish test 2026-10-12, papyrus-production 712236451410, account asserted before every call] Method: invoked each site's content-actions Lambda with the AppSync event shape {fieldName: saveItemDraft|publishItem|unpublishItem, arguments:{input:<json string>}, identity:{username}}; counts via IAM-signed GraphQL list queries over every model. Baselines in /Users/home/Projects/.baselines/publish-test-20261012/ (counts-before/after).
RESULTS: all three Lambdas returned ok with no errors (no 'Unable to find aws', no AccessDenied). Counts before == after for all three sites. Test items deleted.
- Pilobol.us: CMS main job 8 SUCCEED before test; Lambda env PAPYRUS_READER_AMPLIFY_APP_ID=dpdg1mg84dlwb, role allows StartJob/ListJobs on apps/dpdg1mg84dlwb/branches/main/jobs/*. Publish -> reader job started automatically (jobId in Lambda result), item page and the /articles listing live at 72-80 s. Unpublish -> job (3m50s this time), listing gone ~131 s after unpublish.
- p.apyr.us: publish result revalidated ok (tags + paths), never-requested URL /information/articles/<slug> 200 at 9 s.
- Threat Intelligence: revalidated ok, /articles/<slug> 200 at 9 s.
- Listings: Pilobol.us lists articles in /articles/index.html and home (rebuilt, so listed at once). Pretext sites list via PublishedEditionItem, so a published item does NOT appear on the home/archive/edition pages without an edition; not tried (no edition publish action in the Lambda).
STALENESS: unpublish on Pretext sites revalidates ok and the Amplify origin returns 404 at once, but the plain URL kept serving 200 for ~3454 s (p.apyr.us) and ~3599 s (TI) = the s-maxage=3600 (+ stale-while-revalidate) that Next sends; the CDN layer in front (Amplify's) is not purged by revalidatePath. Pilobol.us: reader edge E2GKJ877IAH2I8 uses Managed-CachingOptimized (not CachingDisabled; all other papyrus-edge dists use CachingDisabled), HTML s-maxage=60 (so ~60 s), BUT Amplify's 301 for a missing .html (Location /articles/<slug>/) carries NO cache-control and CachingOptimized defaults to 24 h: a URL probed before publishing keeps returning 301->404 for up to 24 h after publish (seen: previous run's slug still 301 after 6300 s, even with ?cb=, query is not in the cache key). Fixes (not implemented): (1) Pretext: send s-maxage=60 (or 300) for HTML at origin; (2) call cloudfront:CreateInvalidation from the publish Lambda on the papyrus-edge-* distributions (E2QW8WOFWQT0H4 p.apyr.us, E20NJAIXZ1WKWD TI, E2GKJ877IAH2I8 pilobol.us reader), needs IAM + env var; (3) Pilobol.us reader: switch to CachingDisabled or a policy with default TTL 60 s, and invalidate on rebuild. Note Amplify-origin cache is not controllable from our edge.
